title: Bram and the Thorn Revisited
premise: Edmund Montrose, a runaway apprentice hiding her hedge-witch gift behind a smuggler's trade in the Thornfell mountains, is captured by the crown's witch-hunters and dragged to the capital. There she discovers the king has been hollowed out by a thorn-crowned entity that feeds on oaths of loyalty, and the only way to free him is an unbinding rite that will cost Edmund her own gift — and perhaps her name itself. Betrayed by the mentor who sold her to save his own skin, and torn between the hunter sworn to deliver her and the truth she owes the realm, Edmund chooses truth over every loyalty she's ever kept. In the end she unbinds the king at the price of her magic and her old identity, walking out of the palace as no one's apprentice, no one's quarry — simply herself.
about_author: G. M. Amberdale is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent years mapping mountain passes before turning to fiction about the people who travel them. They write fantasy rooted in folk magic, hard roads, and the quiet cost of doing what is right.

chapters.title: Salt Roads
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. She runs contraband charms through Thornfell's smuggler paths, keeping her gift buried deep. When crown riders sweep the pass hunting 'the gifted,' her mentor Aldous sells her location to buy his own safety. The beat: comfortable isolation shattering into betrayal.

chapters.title: The Iron Warrant
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Captured by witch-hunter Captain Serah Vane, who is unsettlingly fair-minded for her office, Edmund hides her power during the road to the capital. She learns the hunt isn't extermination — it's conscription. Beat: fear tempered by grudging curiosity about her captor.

chapters.title: A Court of Oaths
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. Arriving in the capital, Serah presents her prisoners while privately doubting the Lord Protector's zeal. Edmund glimpses the king at court: a man whose eyes are wrong, crowned in living blackthorn. Beat: dread crystallizing into purpose.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing Him
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Forced to serve as a scrying asset, Edmund touches the king's mind and finds him entombed inside himself, whispering one word: unbind. The thorn-entity notices her touch. Beat: horror mixed with the first spark of resolve.

chapters.title: What Aldous Knew
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Reunited with Aldous in the cells, she learns he once served the previous royal hedge-witch — the woman who bound the thorn-thing to the king in the first place, and died for it. He gives her half the rite. Beat: rage softening toward grief and understanding.

chapters.title: Loyalty Is a Leash
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. The Lord Protector orders Serah to execute the prisoners once their usefulness ends. Torn between her oath and mounting evidence of the king's possession, Serah chooses to warn Edmund. Beat: duty cracking under the weight of truth.

chapters.title: Thornfall
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Escape through the palace's forgotten ways, guided by the king's fading whispers. Aldous dies holding the gate so they can flee, redeeming his betrayal. Beat: loss sharpening commitment; the fugitives become allies.

chapters.title: The Rite of Unbinding
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. In the old queen's ruined chapel, Edmund completes the rite from Aldous's notes and her own instinct: it requires the caster's gift as fuel — permanently. Serah stands guard against the hunters closing in. Beat: quiet acceptance of sacrifice.

chapters.title: Crown of Ash
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Climax: Edmund confronts the thorn-entity in the throne room, offering her magic to pull it out of the king. Serah breaks her final oath by turning her blade on the Lord Protector. The king wakes; the thing burns. Beat: love and loyalty remade through truth.

chapters.title: No One's Apprentice
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Magicless but free, Edmund declines the restored king's offer of a place at court. She and Serah take the salt road back to Thornfell together, not master and prisoner but equals. Beat: identity found not in power, but in choice.
